clue.text: Roam around in round H

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other, the rearranged letters within the sphere

parts.note: a ball is a round object

indicators.note: around signals the letters of roam being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to wander about inside a circle marked H.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle H stands for a hat. 'around' turns ROAM into MORA, which goes inside BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, a kind of headgear named after the royal castle.

clue.text: He can produce a China man's H

definitions.text: He can produce a China man
definitions.meaning: in cricket a chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spin delivery, which only one kind of player sends down
a hat, as throughout this puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a left-arm unorthodox spin ball; the player who delivers it is a bowler, which is also a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer delivering the ball, and also a hard felt hat with a rounded crown.

clue.text: Soon the French combine to undo the knot

indicators.note: combine tells you the letters are mixed together

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Soon the French couple will untie the knot, ending the marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a knot is to slacken it and begin to untie it.

clue.text: Old sibling round a place of refreshment

indicators.note: round says those letters go around the single letter

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: An elderly sister seated around a cafe table.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert with water, so a welcome stop for travellers.

clue.text: Fish can be cooked at house very heartlessly

indicators.note: be cooked means the letters of can are messed about
heartlessly means the middle letters of very are removed

explanation.surface: Tinned fish may be cooked at home very carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be cooked' rearranges CAN into ANC; 'heartlessly' takes ER out of VERY to leave VY.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy is a small salty sea fish, often tinned.

clue.text: To bear off H

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters of to bear are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry something away from a spot marked H.
explanation.walkthrough: H stands for a hat throughout this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a stiff straw hat with a flat crown, worn at regattas.

clue.text: Buy in too many cattle?

parts.note: the first part defines a shop ordering excess goods; read again as two words, the clue describes having more livestock than needed

explanation.walkthrough: Livestock is stock, so a farmer with surplus cattle has an excess of it, the same word as buying in more supplies than you can sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay in more supplies than needed, with a nod to a farmer's livestock.

clue.text: Choir act, suffering on the chest

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters of choir act are in distress and rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir's performance suffers from chest trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoracic means relating to the thorax, the upper trunk of the body.

clue.text: Genuine stretch in computer system

parts.note: real means genuine
a stretch is a period of time, especially in prison

explanation.surface: A genuine spell working inside a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A real-time system processes data the instant it arrives, with no delay.

clue.text: Parliamentary seat

parts.note: reads like a constituency won at an election, but means a literal cushion in the House of Lords stuffed with fleece

explanation.walkthrough: A 'seat' in Parliament usually means a constituency; here it is a piece of furniture, the Lord Speaker's wool-filled cushion in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The large red cushion stuffed with fleece on which the Lord Speaker sits in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Iron Lady's H

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name, standing in for any lady

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, and something of hers marked H.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' suggests Thatcher, but it splits into iron (FE) and a lady's name (DORA). H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim.

clue.text: New arts supremo

indicators.note: new signals the letters of arts given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly appointed head of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar is a Russian emperor, and figuratively anyone placed in overall charge.

clue.text: Some resin damaged more than one coming out

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of some resin are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A batch of resin is spoiled, and more than one piece emerges.
explanation.definitionFit: An emersion is an emergence, such as a star reappearing after an eclipse, so the plural is several emergings.

clue.text: Second handle on the pole

parts.note: a haft is the handle of a knife or axe

explanation.surface: Fixing a second handle onto a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a long rod, as in the pole of a cart or the stem of a spear.

clue.text: Like dust on a lot of coconuts

parts.note: a coconut shy is a fairground stall with a row of coconuts on posts to throw balls at

explanation.surface: Dust settling on a heap of coconuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game where players throw balls to knock coconuts off stands, so the shy is the lot of coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means covered in or resembling ash, the powdery residue, so like dust.

clue.text: Peter's worried about accepting an honour at such a time

indicators.note: accepting says the jumbled letters take in the honour
worried means agitated, so the letters of Peter are shaken up

parts.note: MBE is Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: Peter is anxious about receiving an honour at a particular time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the letters of Peter's (the apostrophe adds nothing but S); 'about' is a link. MBE is a British honour given in the New Year and Birthday lists.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth month of the year is a particular time, a period in the calendar.

clue.text: Carelessly hid nothing inside strange element

indicators.note: inside says the jumbled letters go within the word for strange

parts.note: rum is a British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters of hid plus the round letter are thrown together anyhow

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone hid nothing carelessly inside a strange substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carelessly' rearranges the clue's hid plus the zero; 'rum' is old British slang for strange, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a silvery metallic chemical element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Nonsense at the Yard over authoritative individual

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the whole run is turned upside down

parts.note: rot means nonsense
Scotland Yard houses the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Rubbish talked at Scotland Yard about a commanding figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROT + AT + CID backwards. Scotland Yard is London's police headquarters, home of the CID.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is an absolute ruler who issues commands, so a domineering person.

clue.text: Diagrams of chaps struggling with rig

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of chaps and rig wrestle into a new order

explanation.surface: Diagrams of men wrestling with an oil rig.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphics are visual images such as charts and illustrations.

clue.text: Breaks in despite broken stirrup?

indicators.note: broken tells you the letters of stirrup are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bursts in on horseback despite a broken stirrup.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force a way into a place, a violent entry.

clue.text: Cries from Patrick Moore's observatory

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run Moore's observatory

explanation.surface: Weeping heard from the astronomer Patrick Moore's observatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick Moore was a British TV astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobs are noisy weeping breaths, so cries in the sense of weeping.

clue.text: H is all right in a sports lesson

indicators.note: in places the okay letters inside the abbreviation for a gym class

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school sports lesson
OK means all right

explanation.surface: An H mark is approved during a school sports lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: H stands for a hat in this puzzle; PE is physical education at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A poke is a bonnet with a projecting brim, a style of Victorian hat.

clue.text: In a spot, having amended bill for H

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the word for spots

parts.note: pox is a disease of spots or pustules

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the letters of bill are rearranged

explanation.surface: In trouble after a bill was altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' turns BILL into ILLB, which goes 'In' POX. H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillbox is a small round brimless hat, famously worn by Jackie Kennedy.

clue.text: Criticise a degree of H

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Disparaging an academic degree in something marked H.
explanation.walkthrough: H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat woven from palm leaves.

clue.text: Willing Lawrence to make a cell

parts.note: game means willing, up for it
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials

explanation.surface: Lawrence is ready to make a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: T.E. Lawrence was the British officer known as Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell such as a sperm or egg.

clue.text: H for leading eggheads

parts.note: top means leading, foremost
the heads of eggs: each egg starts with E, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: A hat awarded to the leading intellectuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggheads' is read as the heads of two eggs, E and E. H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a lightweight pith helmet worn for shade in hot countries.

clue.text: Airline call out: "Miss Gardner's H!"

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of call are rearranged

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: An airline announcement shouts out that an item marked H belongs to actress Ava Gardner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns CALL into LACL. H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A balaclava is a knitted woollen hood covering the head and neck, named after a Crimean battle.

clue.text: At home, having tea outside with a friend

indicators.note: outside says the tea letters wrap around the home letters

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
in means at home

explanation.surface: At home, having tea with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' gives mate, a pal.

clue.text: Attempt to put in one pound for H

indicators.note: to put in says the next pieces are placed within the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: An effort to spend a single pound on something marked H.
explanation.walkthrough: H stands for a hat in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and indented crown.

clue.text: Jack might give letters, taking time out to give up power

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: taking with out, around the word time, says that letter is removed
out completes taking out, the removal signal

parts.note: to dictate is to give letters to a secretary to write down

explanation.surface: A sailor dictating his letters takes time off before resigning his command.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is short for jack tar, a sailor, giving the able seaman; 'taking time out' removes a single T from the word for giving letters to a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or office, formally relinquishing authority.

clue.text: Give fresh classification to seaside town

definitions.meaning: a holiday place by the sea

explanation.surface: Reclassifying a coastal holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort again (re-sort) for the first; a holiday destination like Brighton for the second.

clue.text: Dig up a form of taxation that former church could accept

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: could accept means the church letters take in the tax letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A former church that could take on a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could accept' puts a VAT inside the Church of England's letters; 'that' is a link, and the former piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excavate is to unearth by digging, as archaeologists do.
